title: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) - Band 28 (700 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) filter targeting Band 28 (700 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on Langasite substrate with a target center frequency of 1317.6 MHz and bandwidth of 206.8 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: Band 28 (700 MHz)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: Langasite
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: Cadence AWR Microwave Office
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design targeting Band 28 (700 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1317.6 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       206.8 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 20.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 48.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 26.0 dB
Q Factor:               3734
Temperature Coefficient:-15.8 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.7 x 2.5 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   11
Electrode Material:     Pt/Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Cadence AWR Microwave Office and load the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Langasite with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1317.6 MHz, BW 206.8 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, Langasite).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N9041B UXA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 3953 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 20.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 310 MHz offset >= 48.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 9 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 2.6 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +30 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 93%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-03-18
Devices Tested:         10
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.21 dB
Return Loss (meas):     21.9 dB
Rejection (meas):       51.3 dB
Isolation (meas):       31.0 dB
Q Factor (meas):        3734
Group Delay Variation:  5.3 ns
Power Handling:         +29 dBm
Die Yield:              81.5%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 28 (700 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) Batch-to-batch reproducibility confirmed over 3 wafer lots.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
